items.q: Match the following GLP-1 agonist to its feature — 1) Exenatide 2) Liraglutide 3) Semaglutide 4) Tirzepatide … A) Twice daily injection B) Once daily injection C) Once weekly oral / injectable D) Dual GLP-1/GIP agonist
items.exp: Exenatide is twice daily; liraglutide is once daily; semaglutide is once weekly oral or injectable; tirzepatide is a dual GLP-1/GIP agonist. (Book p929)

items.q: A patient on a GLP-1 agonist develops acute abdominal pain with elevated lipase. The most consistent drug class complication is:
items.exp: GLP-1 agonists (especially exenatide) carry a class warning for acute pancreatitis. (Book p929)

items.q: Assess GLP-1 agonists: I They cause glucose-dependent insulin secretion. II They promote glucagon release in hypoglycaemia.
items.exp: GLP-1 agonists stimulate insulin and suppress glucagon in a glucose-dependent manner, limiting hypoglycaemia. (Book p929)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a non-GLP-1 injectable hypoglycaemic agent?
items.exp: Tirzepatide is a dual GLP-1/GIP agonist; the others are basal insulin analogues. (Book p929)

items.q: The dual incretin agonist tirzepatide combines GLP-1 agonism with ___ agonism.
items.exp: Tirzepatide combines GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonism, producing greater HbA1c reduction and weight loss than GLP-1 agonists alone. (Book p929)

items.q: Match the following GLP-1 agonist to its main clinical strength — 1) Liraglutide 2) Semaglutide 3) Exenatide LAR 4) Dulaglutide … A) Cardiovascular outcome trial benefit B) HbA1c and weight loss C) Once-weekly injectable D) Easy-to-use pen
items.exp: Liraglutide has landmark cardiovascular outcome data; semaglutide produces the largest HbA1c and weight loss; exenatide LAR is once-weekly; dulaglutide offers a simple weekly pen. (Book p929)

items.q: A patient with T2DM and CKD benefits from a GLP-1 agonist. Which renal protective mechanism is most cited?
opts: Improvement in albuminuria and slowing of GFR decline
items.exp: GLP-1 agonists reduce albuminuria and slow GFR decline via metabolic and haemodynamic effects. (Book p929)

items.q: Assess GLP-1 adverse effects: I Nausea is common, especially with dose escalation. II GLP-1 agonists are contraindicated in pregnancy.
items.exp: Nausea is common during titration; GLP-1 agonists are not approved in pregnancy and are stopped before conception. (Book p929)

items.q: Match the following GLP-1 / GIP property — 1) Source of exenatide 2) Source of liraglutide 3) Liraglutide modification 4) Semaglutide modification … A) Exendin-4 from Gila monster B) Modified GLP-1 analogue C) C16 fatty-acid side chain for albumin binding D) Similar acylation for half-life extension
items.exp: Exenatide is derived from exendin-4 (Gila monster); liraglutide is a modified GLP-1 with a fatty acid side chain for albumin binding; semaglutide has similar acylation to extend half-life. (Book p929)

items.q: A patient develops medullary thyroid carcinoma while on a GLP-1 agonist. The most consistent mechanism is:
items.exp: GLP-1 receptor activation on thyroid C-cells produces calcitonin release and may contribute to C-cell hyperplasia in rodents. (Book p929)

items.q: Tirzepatide's effect on weight is most consistent with ___ levels of weight loss in trials.
items.exp: Tirzepatide produces greater weight loss than GLP-1 agonists alone, with some patients achieving >15% weight reduction. (Book p929)

items.q: Assess GLP-1 / GIP cardiovascular outcome trials: I Liraglutide reduced MACE in high-risk patients. II Semaglutide showed cardiovascular benefit in the SUSTAIN-6 trial.
items.exp: LEADER (liraglutide) and SUSTAIN-6 (semaglutide) both showed cardiovascular benefit in high-risk T2DM. (Book p929)
